key_insight: Parallel pairwise entangling gates across neighboring trapped-ion wells can implement a transversal controlled-Z operation while suppressing unwanted couplings.
engineering_relevance: For selected register sizes, geometric cancellation enables faster parallel operation than sequential two-qubit gates while requiring a significantly smaller two-photon Rabi frequency.
method: Couple corresponding ion pairs across a double-well architecture.
Suppress unwanted couplings using tailored dynamical decoupling with quadratically scaling pulse count.
Use geometric cancellation to reduce pulse requirements.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes decoherence and laser-misalignment crosstalk, then evaluates crosstalk-induced errors during fault-tolerant logical Bell-state preparation between two [[4,1,2]] code blocks.
watch_item: Laser alignment and decoherence remain implementation concerns, and the reported speed advantage applies only to selected register sizes.
paper_title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing
